thread.title: Apple: Tablet Market Share Rises in the First Quarter

author: David Marino-Nachison
title: Apple: Tablet Market Share Rises in the First Quarter
text:
Photo: Getty Images By David Marino-Nachison May 3, 2018 11:32 a.m. ET
Apple extended its lead in tablet market share in the first quarter even as its latest device, a new $329 iPad, launched in late March, according to new data.
Barron’s Next 50 company Apple (AAPL) shipped 9.1 million iPads in Q1, according to IDC , up from 8.9 million a year ago. That was good for nearly 29% of the market, marking an increase from just below 25% in 2017. Apple’s new $329 iPad, seen by many reviewers as more of an update than a completely new model, came out toward the end of March.
Apple managed just below 27% of tablet market share in 2017, according to IDC .
Newsletter Sign-up Globally, total tablet shipments came in at 31.7 million, down from 35.8 million in 2017. But tablets with detachable keyboards grew nearly 3% year-over-year, according to IDC, representing more than 15% of all tablet shipments.
Also noteworthy in Q1: The arrival of the first tablets to run the Alphabet -owned (GOOGL) Chrome operating system, which also happened in March . “Chrome OS’ entrance in the detachable market is a welcome change as Google is finally a serious contender from a platform perspective,” said IDC’s Jitesh Ubrani in a statement.
Samsung maintained its number-two spot with market share at 16.7%; its shipments fell to 5.3 million from 6 million a year earlier. Huawei saw shipments rise 13% year-over-year to 3.2 million, with IDC citing growth in Europe. Amazon.com (AMZN) slipped to fifth place, just below Lenovo.
We covered IDC’s first-quarter stats on the smartphone market yesterday.
